lines.text: In the eighteen thirties, tomatoes were sold as medicine.
lines.caption: In the 1830s, tomatoes were sold as medicine.

lines.text: And the pills had a shocking secret.
In eighteen thirty-four, a doctor named John Cook Bennett claimed tomatoes could treat diarrhea, indigestion and headaches, and even prevent cholera.
lines.caption: In 1834, a doctor named John Cook Bennett claimed tomatoes could treat diarrhea, indigestion and headaches, and even prevent cholera.

lines.text: Soon, tomato pills were everywhere, promising to cure almost anything.
Two sellers fought in the newspapers for two years, each calling the other a fraud.
Then people tested the pills. There was no tomato in them at all. They were basically laxatives.
